text: dsh-mood 是 DeepSeek Harness 的 Web 插件，把会话中的工具失败、重复调用和活动情况汇总为 GOOD、CONFUSED、FRUSTRATED、OVERWHELMED 四种行为状态，并通过 mood 投影提供当前状态、变化原因和会话轨迹。它由宿主折叠会话事件，浏览器客户端在会话头部工具栏显示状态灯，悬停可查看轨迹。阈值可在插件配置中调整；连续成功后恢复状态，并对重复原因设置冷却。适合想快速查看编码 agent 是否反复失败或重复操作的 DSH Web 用户。状态保存在运行时内存中，不需要额外 API 密钥。

dsh-mood derives four agent behavior states from tool failures, repetition, and activity. The host exposes a mood projection; the web client shows status and session journey in the session header. Thresholds are configurable, recovery requires consecutive successes, and no API key is needed.
想在 DSH 会话头部快速看到 agent 最近是否顺利
连续报错时能不能给我一个醒目的状态提示

让 DSH 根据工具调用表现显示一个简单的状态灯
怎么快速知道编码 agent 是不是陷入反复失败
希望看到当前会话状态以及它一路如何变化
Show me at a glance when my coding agent keeps failing.
Can the session header display a status based on repeated tool calls?
dsh-mood 的功能「四态行为指示」：宿主根据连续失败、同一工具重复次数和活动信号折叠会话事件，计算 GOOD、CONFUSED、FRUSTRATED 或 OVERWHELMED 状态，并提供固定原因。
dsh-mood 的功能「会话头部状态灯」：Web 客户端读取 mood 投影，在会话头部工具栏显示当前状态及近期变化原因；状态轨迹可悬停查看。
dsh-mood 的功能「可调判定阈值」：可配置重复次数、失败次数、活动信号数、恢复成功数、冷却时间和检测窗口等正整数阈值。
dsh-mood 的功能「状态快照与变化事件」：宿主提供按会话读取 mood 快照的接口，并在状态变化时发出 mood/change 事件，供其他宿主侧消费者使用。
dsh-mood 的行为状态只保存在运行时内存，会话重启后不保留此前的状态轨迹；README 也说明公开 npm 客户端缺少所需 Web API，独立浏览器安装暂不可用。

dsh-mood

A tiny mood ring for your AI coding agent.
@dsh-external/dsh-mood README · Introduction：

@dsh-external/dsh-mood README · Introduction：

中文

> *"Your agent doesn't have feelings. But its behavior does. It's not science. It's a mood ring."* dsh-mood watches how your AI coding agent is working — consecutive failures, repeating the same tool, activity level — and folds that into one simple four-state Mood, shown as a **low-friction status light** in the session header: doing fine 😊, confused 😕, frustrated 😤, overwhelmed 🤯. Machine-readable project facts: [llms.txt](llms.txt)

@dsh-external/dsh-mood README · 30-second proof：After installing and refreshing `dsh web`, a status light appears beside the session header. Have the agent fail a few times and watch it go 😊 → 😤; a run of stable successes brings it back to 😊:

| Without dsh-mood | With `dsh-mood` |
| --- | --- |
| You guess whether the agent is fine or stuck by reading the log. | At a glance you see the current Mood, a verifiable why (e.g. `3 consecutive failures`), and the session's mood journey. |

@dsh-external/dsh-mood README · Why Mood?：Coding agents are good at moving quickly — and just as good at getting stuck. Consecutive failures, repeating the same call, several abnormal signals at once. While you wait, the one thing you want to know is: *does it look OK right now?*

Mood is not magic. It is an **interpretable behavior classification**. Every Mood comes from observed signals and gives you a fixed, verifiable why. It never interrupts the workflow and never pretends to measure the model's inner psychology.

@dsh-external/dsh-mood README · The four Moods：| Mood | Meaning | Observed signal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 😊 **GOOD** | Everything looks fine | steady useful results, no abnormal repetition |
| 😕 **CONFUSED** | Starting to spin | repeating the same / highly similar action |
| 😤 **FRUSTRATED** | Failing visibly | a short run of clear consecutive failures |
| 🤯 **OVERWHELMED** | Out of control / overloaded | high activity + failure + repetition together |

@dsh-external/dsh-mood README · The four Moods：When several hold at once, priority is: `🤯 OVERWHELMED > 😤 FRUSTRATED > 😕 CONFUSED > 😊 GOOD`. A normal, complex task is **not** flagged OVERWHELMED just for many tool calls — it requires several abnormal signals together.

@dsh-external/dsh-mood README · Anti-flash design：- **Upgrades are sensitive.** A failure/repeat crossing its threshold moves the Mood up immediately.
- **Recovery is conservative.** Returning to GOOD needs a few consecutive successes, so a single success doesn't make it bounce.
- **Reasons are de-duplicated.** The same reason stops re-surfacing within its cooldown window, but a real recovery or worse escalation is never hidden.
- **Session journey.** It remembers the whole trip (`😊 → 😤 → 😊`), shown on hover.

@dsh-external/dsh-mood README · Install from a Release package：```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest `
  -Uri 'https://github.com/Raphaelutumn/dsh-mood/releases/latest/download/dsh-external-dsh-mood-0.1.0.tgz' `
  -OutFile '.\dsh-mood-0.1.0.tgz'

When running from a DeepSeek Harness source checkout:

```powershell
$env:DSH_HOME='D:\Deepseek harness\.dsh'
corepack pnpm --dir 'D:\Deepseek harness' dsh plugin --profile web add .\dsh-mood-0.1.0.tgz
```

@dsh-external/dsh-mood README · Build from source：```powershell
git clone https://github.com/Raphaelutumn/dsh-mood.git
Set-Location .\dsh-mood
corepack pnpm install
corepack pnpm pack --pack-destination .

@dsh-external/dsh-mood README · Uninstall：```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-mood
```

> If you run the DeepSeek Harness monorepo directly, the two packages `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mood` (host) and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-mood` (client) are already wired into `dsh-base` / `dsh-web-app` and load with the default profile.

@dsh-external/dsh-mood README · Configuration：| Field | Default | Meaning |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `confusedRepeatThreshold` | `3` | consecutive occurrences of one tool that mean CONFUSED |
| `frustratedFailureThreshold` | `3` | consecutive failures that mean FRUSTRATED |
| `overwhelmedSignalCount` | `3` | whether high activity + failure + repetition are all present for OVERWHELMED |
| `stableSuccessesToRecover` | `2` | consecutive successes required to return to GOOD |
| `changeCooldownMs` | `60000` | how long before the same reason stops re-surfacing |
| `repetitionWindow` | `12` | recent tool calls kept for repeat detection |
| `highActivityThreshold` | `4` | window length treated as "high activity" |

@dsh-external/dsh-mood README · Configuration：Override in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: mood
  config:
    frustratedFailureThreshold: 5
    stableSuccessesToRecover: 3

All config values must be positive integers. Invalid config fails plugin load loudly rather than silently weakening behavior.

@dsh-external/dsh-mood README · Compatibility：| Environment | Support & verification |
| --- | --- |
| Node.js 20 / 22 / 24 | matches DeepSeek Harness |
| DeepSeek Harness | host `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mood` + client `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-mood`; standalone `@dsh-external/dsh-mood` |
| Session header UI | `conversation.session.header.utilities` slot (right-aligned, additive, never pollutes the message flow) |

@dsh-external/dsh-mood README · What the model sees：Mood is a **pure observer**: it changes no model request, adds no prompt, and vetoes no tool. `ctx.mood.snapshot(session)` reads the current snapshot; `mood/change` events notify host-side consumers when the Mood changes.

@dsh-external/dsh-mood README · Does it interrupt the agent?：No. It is a read-only behavior observer — no injected prompts, no call vetoing or rewriting. The status light lives only in the session header and never touches the message flow.

@dsh-external/dsh-mood README · Is it rigorous science?：No. Mood is an **interpretable behavior classification**; every why comes from observed signals. It does not pretend to measure the model's mental state.

@dsh-external/dsh-mood README · Why does recovery need several successes?：To avoid flipping on success/failure alternation. Upgrades are sensitive, recovery is conservative — that is the core anti-flash design.
